packet.headline_seed: Argentina face fine for Falklands banner in semi-final win
packet.description_seed: Argentina face the prospect of a Fifa fine after their players celebrated the World Cup semi-final win against England with a banner in support of their country's claims to the Falkland Islands.

what: Argentina face fine for Falklands banner in semi-final win

clean_source_blocks.text: Argentina's players display their controversial banner after their win over England Argentina face the prospect of a Fifa fine after their players celebrated the World Cup semi-final win against England with a banner in support of their country's claims to the Falkland Islands. The defending world champions produced a dramatic late comeback in Atlanta, scoring twice to defeat Thomas Tuchel's side 2-1 and book a showdown with Spain in Sunday's final. After the final whistle, their players were seen celebrating while holding a banner reading "Las Malvinas son Argentinas", which translates as "The Falklands are Argentine". The UK and Argentina went to war over the Falklands, an archipelago in the South Atlantic Ocean that has been a British Overseas Territory since 1833, from April to June 1982.
Argentina face the prospect of a Fifa fine after their players celebrated the World Cup semi-final win against England with a banner in support of their country's claims to the Falkland Islands.

Argentinian players celebrated beating England in the World Cup semi-final with a banner reading “The Malvinas are Argentine” in a reference to the Falkland Islands. Tottenham midfielder Giovani Lo Celso was among those holding the sign as his teammates danced on the pitch after their 2-1 win over the Three Lions in Atlanta on Wednesday. Political slogans are banned from being displayed on the pitch or on players’ equipment according to Fifa rules. Tension had again been building before the match over the sovereignty of the Falklands, an archipelago in the South Atlantic Ocean, 300 miles off the coast of Argentina which have been a British Overseas Territory since 1833.

Argentina believes the group of islands, situated 300 miles off its east coast, should have sovereignty. The 74-day conflict led to the deaths of 655 Argentine and 255 British servicemen. Three people from the islands also died. In 2014, Fifa fined the Argentine Football Association £20,000 after its players held up a banner with the same message before a friendly against Slovenia. World football's governing body said the gesture breached rules on political action and team misconduct. England suffer World Cup semi-final heartbreak with loss to Argentina Before the last-four tie, Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni had said he was "not going to mix" football and politics. "The reality is that this is a football match. I can't mix things up, especially out of respect for what happened so many years ago," Scaloni had said.

payload.title: Argentiinaa uhkaa FIFA-sakko Falklandinsaariin liittyvästä kyltistä
payload.summary: Argentiinan pelaajat juhlivat Englannista otettua MM-välierävoittoa Falklandinsaarten suvereniteettia koskevalla kyltillä. Poliittiset iskulauseet ovat FIFA:n sääntöjen vastaisia.
payload.content:
Argentiinan jalkapalloliittoa saattaa uhata FIFA:n sakko, kun maajoukkueen pelaajat juhlivat Englannista otettua 2–1-välierävoittoa Falklandinsaarten suvereniteettia koskevalla poliittisella kyltillä. Kyltti nostettiin esiin Atlantan kentällä loppuvihellyksen jälkeen, ja siinä tuettiin Argentiinan vaatimusta Britannian hallitsemiin saariin.

## Poliittinen viesti nousi esiin voitonjuhlissa

Hallitseva maailmanmestari Argentiina nousi ottelun loppuhetkillä tappioasemasta voittoon kahdella maalilla ja eteni sunnuntain MM-finaaliin Espanjaa vastaan. Pelaajien tanssiessa kentällä osa joukkueesta piti kylttiä, jossa luki espanjaksi ”Las Malvinas son Argentinas” eli ”Malvinassaaret kuuluvat Argentiinalle”. Tottenhamin keskikenttäpelaaja Giovani Lo Celso oli yksi kylttiä kannatelleista pelaajista.

Voitto syntyi dramaattisesti, sillä Argentiina teki molemmat maalinsa ottelun lopussa. Tulos päätti Englannin turnauksen välierään ja vei Argentiinan tavoittelemaan uutta maailmanmestaruutta.

FIFA:n sääntöjen mukaan poliittisia iskulauseita ei saa näyttää kentällä eikä pelaajien varusteissa. Siksi Argentiinan jalkapalloliitto voi joutua kurinpitotoimien kohteeksi. Kyse ei olisi ensimmäisestä vastaavasta tapauksesta. FIFA määräsi vuonna 2014 Argentiinan liitolle 20 000 punnan sakon, kun maajoukkueen pelaajat esittelivät samalla viestillä varustettua kylttiä ennen Sloveniaa vastaan pelattua ystävyysottelua. FIFA katsoi tuolloin eleen rikkoneen poliittista toimintaa ja joukkueen käytöstä koskevia sääntöjä.

Ennen välierää Argentiinan päävalmentaja Lionel Scaloni sanoi, ettei hän aio sekoittaa jalkapalloa ja politiikkaa. Hänen mukaansa kyse oli jalkapallo-ottelusta, ja vuosikymmenten takaisia tapahtumia piti kunnioittaa.

## Saarikiistan taustalla on vuoden 1982 sota

Falklandinsaaret sijaitsevat Etelä-Atlantilla noin 480 kilometrin päässä Argentiinan itärannikosta. Saariryhmä on ollut Britannian merentakainen alue vuodesta 1833, mutta Argentiina katsoo suvereniteetin kuuluvan itselleen ja käyttää saarista nimeä Malvinassaaret. Kiista oli kiristänyt tunnelmaa jo ennen keskiviikon välierää.

Britannia ja Argentiina kävivät saarista huhtikuusta kesäkuuhun 1982 sodan, joka kesti 74 päivää. Konfliktissa kuoli 655 argentiinalaista ja 255 brittiläistä sotilasta sekä kolme saarten asukasta. Pelaajien juhlintaan tuoma viesti palautti yhä ratkaisemattoman suvereniteettikiistan näkyvästi jalkapallon MM-turnauksen yhteyteen.
summary_bullets: Argentiina voitti Englannin MM-välierässä 2–1 ja eteni Espanjaa vastaan pelattavaan finaaliin.
Pelaajat esittelivät ottelun jälkeen Argentiinan aluevaatimusta tukevan kyltin.
FIFA sakotti Argentiinan liittoa samasta viestistä vuonna 2014.
payload.journalist_note: Ottelun tapahtumat ja kyltin sisältö ovat yhtenevät kahdessa lähteessä. Mahdollinen FIFA-seuraamus on vielä ennakoitu eikä vahvistettu.

Argentina's players display their controversial banner after their win over England Argentina face the prospect of a Fifa fine after their players celebrated the World Cup semi-final win against England with a banner in support of their country's claims to the Falkland Islands. The defending world champions produced a dramatic late comeback in Atlanta, scoring twice to defeat Thomas Tuchel's side 2-1 and book a showdown with Spain in Sunday's final. After the final whistle, their players were seen celebrating while holding a banner reading "Las Malvinas son Argentinas", which translates as "The Falklands are Argentine". The UK and Argentina went to war over the Falklands, an archipelago in the South Atlantic Ocean that has been a British Overseas Territory since 1833, from April to June 1982.

Argentina face the prospect of a Fifa fine after their players celebrated the World Cup semi-final win against England with a banner in support of their country's claims to the Falkland Islands.

Argentinian players celebrated beating England in the World Cup semi-final with a banner reading “The Malvinas are Argentine” in a reference to the Falkland Islands. Tottenham midfielder Giovani Lo Celso was among those holding the sign as his teammates danced on the pitch after their 2-1 win over the Three Lions in Atlanta on Wednesday. Political slogans are banned from being displayed on the pitch or on players’ equipment according to Fifa rules. Tension had again been building before the match over the sovereignty of the Falklands, an archipelago in the South Atlantic Ocean, 300 miles off the coast of Argentina which have been a British Overseas Territory since 1833.

Argentina believes the group of islands, situated 300 miles off its east coast, should have sovereignty. The 74-day conflict led to the deaths of 655 Argentine and 255 British servicemen. Three people from the islands also died. In 2014, Fifa fined the Argentine Football Association £20,000 after its players held up a banner with the same message before a friendly against Slovenia. World football's governing body said the gesture breached rules on political action and team misconduct. England suffer World Cup semi-final heartbreak with loss to Argentina Before the last-four tie, Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni had said he was "not going to mix" football and politics. "The reality is that this is a football match. I can't mix things up, especially out of respect for what happened so many years ago," Scaloni had said.
